criteria.text: Old keys cease to validate after the documented grace period; active requests and rolling deployments work during rotation; failure and rollback cases are tested without exposing keys.
Record sanitized test evidence and the tested revision, and update relevant documentation.

findings.summary: Risk: any non-zero grace below ~130 s (60 s capability lifetime + 70 s accepted skew) is accepted although the docs say the grace must cover them; a short non-zero grace silently fails in-flight capabilities during a rollout. confidence: medium
findings.evidence: backend/src/main/java/io/github/stevdrey/dokene/tenant/persistence/jpa/TenantContextSigningKeyCallback.java parseRetirementGrace (accepts 0s..7d) vs docs/architecture/tenant-isolation-rls-recipe.md Key Rotation Lifecycle paragraph on grace coverage

findings.summary: The verification record names b24af99 for the first results and only 'the working tree of the review follow-up commit' for the final results, so the final tested revision is not identified by hash.

limitations: Adversarial pass ran for triggers Tenant isolation (V39__retire_superseded_tenant_context_signing_keys.sql verifiers; TenantContextSigningKeyCallback.java), Concurrency (TenantContextSigningKeyCallback.java table lock and transaction) and Migrations (V39 backfill and REVOKE). Hypotheses H1 and H2 were probed and not broken; no pass finding.
H2 probe was not negative-controlled (zero grace also marks the key RETIRED, so removing one guard would not make it fail cheaply).

Unexamined hypotheses: V39 backfill of a pre-existing RETIRED row on an upgraded database; previous-release migration job run against the V39 schema during a release rollback (documented in the runbook; reasoned from code only).
Full backend check/build was not run by instruction (only --tests filters); no live multi-replica Compose rotation was run.
Phase A findings F1 and F2 are not restated by the pass.
remainingActions: Optionally enforce or warn on a non-zero grace below the capability lifetime plus skew (F1).
